outcome: Time of the first stage of labor
Time of the second stage of labor
Time of the total stage of labor
Pregnancy success of VBAC pregnant women
cohort: The study analyzed clinical data from 166 pregnant women attempting Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC) between January 2017 and March 2020.
finding: Oxytocin usage in VBAC pregnant women may increase labor duration, but for those with poor uterine contraction, increasing the dose up to 4-18 mU/min can speed up labor without increasing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: For VBAC pregnant women, oxytocin usage may increase labor duration, but higher doses can safely accelerate labor for those with poor uterine contraction without increasing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes during attempted vaginal delivery.
gest_age: Gestational age was analyzed as an influencing factor (<=40 weeks for pregnancy success) and was found to be significantly different between oxytocin and non-oxytocin groups.
